hints: Use $v = u + at$ for the initial phase with $u = 0$, $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $t = 5\text{ s}$ to find the greatest speed.
Find the deceleration time to rest using $v = u - at$: $0 = 2 - 0.2t_3 \implies t_3 = 10\text{ s}$.
Sketch a trapezium graph starting at $(0,0)$, rising to $(5,2)$, flat until $t = 30$, and descending to rest at $t = 40$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the maximum speed reached during the acceleration phase:
$$v_{\text{max}} = u + at = 0 + 0.4(5) = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the duration of the deceleration phase to rest:
$$v = u - at \implies 0 = 2 - 0.2t_3 \implies t_3 = \frac{2}{0.2} = 10\text{ s}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 5 + 25 + 10 = 40\text{ s}$$

The velocity-time graph is a trapezium with vertices at:
$$(0, 0),\quad (5, 2),\quad (30, 2),\quad (40, 0)$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the constant acceleration equation linking final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and time:
$$v = u + at$$

In the first phase, the elevator starts from rest ($u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and accelerates at $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$v_{\text{max}} = 0 + (0.4)(5) = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The elevator maintains this constant speed for $25\text{ s}$, reaching time $t = 5 + 25 = 30\text{ s}$.

During the final phase, it decelerates at $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until coming to rest ($v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$v = u + at$$
$$0 = 2 - 0.2t_3$$
$$0.2t_3 = 2 \implies t_3 = \frac{2}{0.2} = 10\text{ s}$$
The total time elapsed at the end of the motion is $30 + 10 = 40\text{ s}$.
The velocity-time graph is a trapezium sitting on the $t$-axis with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(5, 2)$, $(30, 2)$, and $(40, 0)$.

hints: Recall that the total distance travelled equals the total area under the velocity-time graph.
Use the trapezium area formula $\text{Area} = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h$ with parallel bases 40 s and 25 s, and height $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total distance as the area of the trapezium under the velocity-time graph:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$$
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(40 + 25)(2) = 65\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Name the foundational graphical principle: the distance travelled is equal to the area under the velocity-time graph.
The graph is a trapezium with parallel horizontal bases of length $40\text{ s}$ (bottom) and $25\text{ s}$ (top), with height $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Write the area formula for a trapezium:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h$$
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{40 + 25}{2} \times 2$$

hints: Apply Newton's second law to the combined system (elevator of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ plus crate of mass $m\text{ kg}$).
Note that while moving upwards and decelerating at $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, the upward acceleration is $-0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system (elevator and crate) during upward deceleration ($a = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$T - (1200 + m)g = (1200 + m)a$$
$$12250 - 10(1200 + m) = -0.2(1200 + m)$$
$$12250 = 9.8(1200 + m)$$

Solve for the mass $m$:
$$1200 + m = \frac{12250}{9.8} = 1250 \implies m = 1250 - 1200 = 50\text{ kg}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Formulate Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ in the upward direction for the combined mass of the elevator ($1200\text{ kg}$) and crate ($m\text{ kg}$):
$$T - M_{\text{total}}g = M_{\text{total}}a$$

During upward deceleration, acceleration is directed downwards: $a = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$12250 - (1200 + m)(10) = (1200 + m)(-0.2)$$
$$12250 - 12000 - 10m = -240 - 0.2m$$
$$250 - 10m = -240 - 0.2m$$

hints: Notice that the contact force on the crate is greatest during upward acceleration ($a = +0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
Apply Newton's second law to the $50\text{ kg}$ crate: $R - mg = ma$.
Substitute $m = 50\text{ kg}$ and $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find $R = 520\text{ N}$, directed upwards.
walkthrough:
Identify that the normal contact force on the crate is greatest when the elevator accelerates upwards ($a = +0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$R - mg = ma$$
$$R - 50(10) = 50(0.4)$$
$$R = 500 + 20 = 520\text{ N}$$

State the direction of the force exerted by the floor on the crate:
$$\text{Direction: upwards}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The force exerted by the floor on the crate is the normal contact reaction force $R$. This force is greatest when the elevator has its maximum upward acceleration ($a = +0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$).

Apply Newton's second law vertically to the $50\text{ kg}$ crate alone:
$$R - mg = ma$$

State the magnitude and direction clearly:
$$\text{Magnitude} = 520\text{ N},\quad \text{Direction: upwards}$$
